To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tripartite of violence, depression and drug use is associated with HIV-risk factors among African American female drug users.

women who had the tripartite of risk factors were more likely than women with one or none to report sexual risk behaviors such as having multiple sex partners, having a history of a sexually transmitted disease, and having an early onset of substance use.
drug users with exposure both to violence and clinical depression are more likely to engage in sexual risk behavior and to have multiple sexual partners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the co-existence of drug use, exposure to violence and clinical depression among a sample of 420 African American female drug users.
the co-occurrence of drug use, depression, and violence among African American women.
the intersection of drug and alcohol use, violence, depression, and sexual risk behavior among African American women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
African American female drug users who have experienced violence, depression and drug use are more likely to engage in risky sexual behavior.
the intersection of drug abuse, violence, and mental health issues among African American women are significant factors in HIV transmission.
the tripartite of risk behaviors (i.e., drug use, violence exposure, and depression) is a risk factor for HIV infection among African American female drug users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women who are exposed to violence and/or clinical depression are at an increased risk to engage in sexual behaviors that place them at risk for HIV infection.
drug users with the full tripartites of HIV-risk are more likely to have more sexual risk behaviors.
women who are exposed to violence and depression, in addition to drug use are at an increased risk to engage in risky sexual behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are numerous obstacles to HIV interventions and that these obstacles may be more pronounced among drug using populations.
women with the full tripartites have a greater number of risk factors and thus, may need more intensive HIV interventions.
there may be a need to provide more comprehensive services to drug users with a history of violence, depression and sexual risk behaviors.
